correctness.rationale: Laga–Shnidman Lemma 7.18 fixes the τ=(x↦−x) bitangent count at four, namely infinity and three horizontal lines, with twelve other τ-pairs. For σ=(y↦ωy), projectively σ-fixed lines are either Y=0 or in the pencil AX+CZ=0. The Y=0 section is the separable quartic x⁴+ax²+b under the discriminant b(a²−4b)≠0; the finite vertical X=uZ section is Z(Y³−f(u)Z³), hence has multiplicities 1+1+1+1 or 1+3 and is never an even bitangent divisor. Infinity Z=0 has intersection 4∞ and is the sole σ-fixed bitangent. Thus n1+2n2=1, n1+3n3=4 and n1+2n2+3n3+6n6=28 give (1,0,1,4). The three horizontals are a size-3 orbit since c³=b−a²/4≠0. Equivariance of τ-pair construction then gives four free µ3-orbits on Prym-related 2-torsion. Independently reproduced discriminant and horizontal square identity; code is a consistency check, not a derivation of Lemma 7.18.

value.rationale: The 28 odd theta characteristics are a canonical geometric invariant of these genus-three curves and the involution/Prym-pair construction is central to their arithmetic study. Classifying the full naturally marked order-six permutation action, including four three-cycles on the 12 Prym-pair set, completes a meaningful symmetry classification. It is neither an arbitrary finite example nor just reiterating the involution count.
residual_risks: Arithmetic Galois orbit structure is not addressed.

final_claim: For smooth bielliptic Picard quartic Y^3 Z=X^4+a X²Z²+b Z⁴ with b(a²−4b)≠0 over algebraically closed field of char≠2,3, the marked µ6 action ζ:(x,y)↦(ζ³x,ζ⁴y) has 28 bitangent orbits 1+3+4×6; only infinity line fixed, three horizontals form one size-three orbit, and the 12 τ-pairs correspond to four µ3 three-cycles in A[2]\A[lambda_hat].
limitations: Geometric statement over algebraically closed characteristic other than 2 and 3, with b(a²−4b)≠0.
Special a=0 full automorphism group may be larger than marked µ6.
